subject.title: feat(gmail): add --inline and --text content modes to gmail attachment

question: Should this PR land both modes, or should it be narrowed to `--inline` while PDF/text extraction is reviewed separately as a core trust boundary?
rationale: The code and proof establish that both modes work, but automation cannot decide whether core should permanently parse hostile document formats and own the added dependency and resource boundary.

options.title: Land inline only
options.body: Keep the narrow remote-client transport fix and move `--text`, the PDF dependency, and the parser subprocess into a separate proposal.

options.title: Accept both modes
options.body: Land the complete feature after explicitly accepting the documented PDF parser and resource-isolation boundary.

recommendation.title: Land inline only
recommendation.body: Keep the narrow remote-client transport fix and move `--text`, the PDF dependency, and the parser subprocess into a separate proposal.

likelyOwner.reason: This is the strongest available broad owner for deciding whether document parsing belongs in the core Gmail CLI surface.
